End-of-Service Gratuity Across the Six GCC Countries

Six countries, six different rules: some use basic salary and some the full wage, and some cut the gratuity on resignation. This comparison puts them side by side.

Prepared and reviewed by the Mustahaqati team · Last updated: 2026-11-03

The rules in brief

CountryRate per yearWage baseCapResignation
UAE21 days for the first 5 years, then 30 daysLast basic salaryTwo years' payNo reduction
Saudi ArabiaHalf a month for the first 5 years, then a monthLast actual wage (with fixed allowances)None0 → ⅓ → ⅔ → full (2/5/10 years)
QatarAt least 21 days (3 weeks)Last basic salaryNoneNo reduction
Kuwait15 days for the first 5 years, then a monthLast full wage with regular allowances18 months' pay0 → ½ → ⅔ → full (3/5/10 years)
OmanA month per year since 31/7/2023 (before: 15 days for the first 3 years, then a month)Last basic salaryNoneNo reduction
BahrainHalf a month for the first 3 years, then a monthLast wage (basic plus social allowance)NoneNo reduction

Rules mainly for non-national private-sector employees; each country has exceptions for nationals and for financial free zones. Details are on each country's calculator page.

A fixed wage of 10,000 in each local currency, whole years, rounded. Kuwait divides the wage by 26, and Oman assumes all service is after 31 July 2023. The figures compare rules, not purchasing power, since the currencies differ.

Three observations

  1. The wage base changes everything: an employee whose basic is half the salary gets half as much in the UAE or Qatar as the same formula gives in Saudi Arabia or Kuwait.
  2. Early resignation is costly only in Saudi Arabia and Kuwait: nothing before 3 years in Kuwait, and before two years in Saudi Arabia.
  3. Systems are moving to savings funds: Bahrain since March 2024, Oman by July 2027 at the latest, the UAE has an optional alternative savings scheme, and Qatar is studying a similar system.

Frequently asked questions

Which Gulf country pays the highest end-of-service gratuity?

Over the long run five countries converge on a month's wage per year after the first years: Oman from the first year since 2023, Bahrain after the third, and the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Kuwait after the fifth, while Qatar stays at 21 days. The bigger difference is the wage base: Saudi Arabia and Kuwait use the wage including fixed allowances, while the UAE, Qatar and Oman use basic salary only. Caps limit the gratuity in the UAE (two years' pay) and Kuwait (18 months).

In which countries does resignation reduce the gratuity?

Saudi Arabia (nothing before two years, then a third, then two thirds, full after 10 years) and Kuwait (nothing before 3 years, then half, then two thirds, full after 10 years). In the UAE, Qatar, Oman and Bahrain resignation does not reduce it.

Are the figures in the table accurate for my case?

The table is illustrative, using a fixed wage of 10,000 and whole years. For Oman it assumes all service is after 31 July 2023, and for Kuwait it divides the wage by 26. Use your country's calculator to enter your own dates and wage.
